lessons.title: Nazra Quran Majeed — Para 13 to Para 20
lessons.notes_html:
This is an oral unit of the book (Nazra and Hifz). There is no written exercise for it in the book; these notes give the facts printed in the book's own pages of this chapter.

What is Nazra?

Nazra means reading the Holy Quran by looking at it. In Class 7, the fixed Nazra portion is eight paras: Para 13 to Para 20. The student reads these paras with correct pronunciation (talaffuz) and tajweed.

The eight paras and their names

  • Para 13 — Wa Ma Ubarri'u
  • Para 14 — Rubama
  • Para 15 — Subhanallazi
  • Para 16 — Qal Alam Aqul
  • Para 17 — Iqtaraba
  • Para 18 — Qad Aflaha
  • Para 19 — Wa Qalallazina
  • Para 20 — Amman Khalaqa

About the Holy Quran (from the chapter's introduction)

  • The Holy Quran is the last Book of Allah, revealed to His last Messenger, Hazrat Muhammad ﷺ.
  • It was revealed in stages over about twenty-three years.
  • The earlier holy books are also mentioned in the Holy Quran.
  • By acting upon the Holy Quran, a person gains success in this world and in the Hereafter.
  • Reciting even one letter of the Holy Quran brings ten rewards.
  • We should read the Holy Quran with tajweed, understand its meaning, and act upon it.

Exam facts given in the book

  • Students should learn the names of their paras by heart.
  • The Nazra and Hifz oral test is held in the mid-term and in the annual examination.
  • Out of the total 100 marks of Islamiat, 40 marks are fixed for the Nazra part.
  • Passing the Nazra Quran is compulsory for passing Islamiat.

mcqs.q: How many paras are fixed for Nazra reading in Class 7 Islamiat?
mcqs.why: The book fixes eight paras for Nazra in Class 7. They run from Para 13 to Para 20, and the student reads them looking at the Holy Quran with correct pronunciation and tajweed.

mcqs.q: The Nazra portion of Class 7 starts from which para?
mcqs.why: The chapter heading itself says: Nazra Quran Majeed — Para 13 to Para 20 (eight paras). So the fixed portion begins at Para 13.

mcqs.q: What is the name of Para 17?
mcqs.why: The book prints the para names in order: 13 Wa Ma Ubarri'u, 14 Rubama, 15 Subhanallazi, 16 Qal Alam Aqul, 17 Iqtaraba, 18 Qad Aflaha, 19 Wa Qalallazina, 20 Amman Khalaqa.

mcqs.q: Para 20 is called:
mcqs.why: Para 20, the last para of the Class 7 Nazra portion, is named Amman Khalaqa, from its opening words. Para 19 is Wa Qalallazina.

mcqs.q: Out of the total 100 marks of Islamiat, how many marks are fixed for the Nazra part?
mcqs.why: The book's instructions for teachers state clearly that out of Islamiat's total 100 marks, 40 marks are fixed for the Nazra part. That is why this oral portion is so important.

mcqs.q: What is compulsory for passing Islamiat?
mcqs.why: The book says passing the Nazra Quran is compulsory (lazmi) in order to pass Islamiat. The oral test of Nazra and Hifz is held in the mid-term and the annual exam.

mcqs.q: Over how many years was the Holy Quran revealed?
mcqs.why: The chapter's introduction tells us the Holy Quran was revealed to Hazrat Muhammad ﷺ in stages, and the period of its revelation is about twenty-three years.

mcqs.q: How much reward is there for reciting one letter of the Holy Quran?
mcqs.why: The introduction of this chapter says that great reward comes from the recitation of the Holy Quran — reciting one letter brings ten rewards (ten nekiyan).

mcqs.q: How should we read the Holy Quran, according to this chapter?
mcqs.why: The book teaches that we should read the Holy Quran Majeed with tajweed, understand its meaning and act upon it, so that we gain success in this world and the Hereafter.

mcqs.q: The Holy Quran is the last Book of Allah, revealed to:
mcqs.why: The chapter begins: the Holy Quran is Allah Almighty's last Book, sent down to His last Messenger, Hazrat Muhammad ﷺ. The earlier holy books are also mentioned in it.

lessons.title: Hifz Quran Majeed — Surah Ad-Duha, Surah Az-Zalzalah, Surah Al-Qaari'ah
lessons.notes_html:
This is an oral unit of the book (Nazra and Hifz). There is no written exercise for it in the book; these notes give the facts printed in the book's own pages of this chapter.

The three surahs to memorize

For Hifz (memorization), the book gives three surahs. Students learn them by heart so that they can recite them in Salah (prayer). The three surahs are:

  • Surah Ad-Duha (11 verses)
  • Surah Az-Zalzalah (8 verses)
  • Surah Al-Qaari'ah (11 verses)

Surah Ad-Duha — main points

  • Allah swears by the morning brightness (Ad-Duha) and by the night when it covers.
  • "Your Lord has not left you, nor is He displeased with you."
  • The Hereafter is better for the Prophet ﷺ than this first (worldly) life, and his Lord will give him so much that he will be pleased.
  • Allah found him an orphan and sheltered him; found him searching (for the path) and guided him; found him poor and made him rich.
  • So: do not oppress the orphan, do not drive away the one who asks, and keep telling others about the blessings of your Lord.

Surah Az-Zalzalah — main points

  • When the earth is shaken with a mighty shaking and throws out its heavy burdens, man will say: "What has happened to it?"
  • On that Day people will come out in groups so that they may be shown their deeds.
  • Whoever does good equal to the weight of an atom (zarrah) will see it; and whoever does evil equal to the weight of an atom will see it.

Surah Al-Qaari'ah — main points

  • Al-Qaari'ah is the striking Day — the Day of Judgement.
  • On that Day, people will be like scattered moths, and the mountains will be like carded wool.
  • The one whose scales (of good deeds) are heavy will live a pleasing life.
  • The one whose scales are light — his home will be Hawiyah, the deep pit of Fire.

mcqs.q: Which three surahs are fixed for Hifz in Class 7?
options: Surah Al-Fil, Surah Quraysh, Surah Al-Ma'un
Surah Ad-Duha, Surah Az-Zalzalah, Surah Al-Qaari'ah
Surah Al-Ikhlas, Surah Al-Falaq, Surah An-Nas
Surah Ya-Sin, Surah Al-Mulk, Surah Ar-Rahman
mcqs.why: The Hifz page of the book is headed: Surah Ad-Duha — Surah Az-Zalzalah — Surah Al-Qaari'ah. These three surahs are memorized so they can be recited in Salah.

mcqs.q: How many verses does Surah Ad-Duha have?
mcqs.why: Counting the verse markers in the book's printed text of Surah Ad-Duha, the surah has 11 verses, ending with the command to proclaim the blessings of one's Lord.

mcqs.q: In Surah Ad-Duha, what does Allah say about the orphan?
options: Give the orphan half your wealth
mcqs.why: Surah Ad-Duha ends with three commands: do not oppress the orphan, do not repel the one who asks (the beggar), and proclaim the blessings of your Lord.

mcqs.q: Surah Ad-Duha tells us that Allah found His Prophet ﷺ an orphan and then:
mcqs.why: The surah says: 'Did He not find you an orphan and shelter you? And He found you searching and guided you. And He found you poor and made you rich.'

mcqs.q: What does 'Az-Zalzalah' describe?
options: A mighty earthquake of the earth
mcqs.why: Surah Az-Zalzalah begins: 'When the earth is shaken with its (mighty) shaking and the earth throws out its burdens.' It describes the earthquake of the Day of Judgement.

mcqs.q: According to Surah Az-Zalzalah, whoever does good equal to the weight of an atom will:
mcqs.why: The surah's last two verses say: whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it. No deed, however small, is lost.

mcqs.q: How many verses are there in Surah Az-Zalzalah?
mcqs.why: The book's printed text of Surah Az-Zalzalah carries 8 verse markers. It is a short surah, ending with the atom's-weight verses.

mcqs.q: What is 'Al-Qaari'ah' in Surah Al-Qaari'ah?
mcqs.why: The surah opens: 'Al-Qaari'ah! What is Al-Qaari'ah? And what will make you know what Al-Qaari'ah is?' — it is the Day when people will be like scattered moths.

mcqs.q: On the Day of Al-Qaari'ah, the mountains will become like:
mcqs.why: Surah Al-Qaari'ah says that on that Day the mountains will be like carded (teased) wool — light and scattered — showing the terror of the Day of Judgement.

mcqs.q: In Surah Al-Qaari'ah, the person whose scales are light will have his home in:
mcqs.why: The surah says: 'As for the one whose scales are heavy, he will be in a pleasing life. And as for the one whose scales are light, his mother (home) will be Hawiyah' — the abyss of Fire.

lessons.title: Hifz and Translation — Two Quranic Duas
lessons.notes_html:
This is an oral unit of the book (Nazra and Hifz). There is no written exercise for it in the book; these notes give the facts printed in the book's own pages of this chapter.

Two Quranic duas to learn with translation

In this part, two verses of the Holy Quran are memorized together with their translation. These duas are recited again and again to gain knowledge and the pleasure of Allah.

Dua 1 — Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 286

"Our Lord! Do not catch hold of us if we forget or make a mistake. Our Lord! Do not put upon us such a burden as You put upon those before us. Our Lord! Do not load us with what we have no strength to bear. Pardon us, forgive us and have mercy on us. You are our Master, so help us against the disbelieving people."

  • In this dua we ask Allah not to punish us for forgetfulness and mistakes.
  • We ask Him not to give us a burden heavier than we can bear.
  • We ask for pardon (mu'afi), forgiveness (bakhshish) and mercy (rahm).
  • We call Allah our Mawla (Master and Helper) and ask His help.

Dua 2 — Surah Ta-Ha, verses 25–28

This is the dua of Hazrat Musa (AS): "My Lord! Open my chest for me, make my work easy for me, and untie the knot from my tongue, so that people may understand my speech."

  • Hazrat Musa (AS) made this dua when Allah sent him to Pharaoh with His message.
  • Students also make this dua for ease in learning and speaking.

Lesson summary printed in the book

  • Reading eight paras (13 to 20) of the Holy Quran as Nazra is necessary.
  • Memorizing Surah Ad-Duha, Surah Az-Zalzalah and Surah Al-Qaari'ah is necessary.
  • The duas told in the Holy Quran in this lesson must be memorized with translation.

mcqs.q: The first dua of this lesson ('Rabbana la tu'akhidhna...') is taken from which surah?
mcqs.why: The book prints this dua with its reference: Al-Baqarah, verse 286. It is the famous closing dua of Surah Al-Baqarah.

mcqs.q: In the dua of Surah Al-Baqarah (286), we ask Allah not to catch hold of us if we:
mcqs.why: The dua begins: 'Our Lord! Do not catch hold of us if we forget (nasiya) or make a mistake (akhta'na).' We ask Allah to overlook our forgetfulness and errors.

mcqs.q: What burden do we ask Allah NOT to put on us in this dua?
options: A burden like the one put on the people before us
mcqs.why: The dua says: 'Our Lord! Do not put upon us a burden (isr) as You put it upon those before us, and do not load us with what we have no strength to bear.'

mcqs.q: The dua of Surah Ta-Ha (verses 25–28) was made by which Prophet?
mcqs.why: 'Rabbi-shrah li sadri' — 'My Lord, open my chest for me' — is the dua of Hazrat Musa (AS), made when Allah sent him to Pharaoh with His message.

mcqs.q: In the dua 'Rabbi-shrah li sadri', what does the Prophet ask Allah to open?
mcqs.why: 'Sharh-e-sadr' means the opening of the chest. Hazrat Musa (AS) asked Allah to open his chest, make his task easy, and untie the knot from his tongue so people would understand his speech.

mcqs.q: Why did Hazrat Musa (AS) ask Allah to untie the knot from his tongue?
options: So that he could read fast
So that he could shout loudly
So that people may understand his speech
mcqs.why: The verse itself gives the reason: 'Yafqahu qawli' — 'so that they may understand my speech.' Clear speech was needed to deliver Allah's message to Pharaoh and his people.

mcqs.q: In the Al-Baqarah dua, Allah is called 'Mawlana'. What does it mean here?
mcqs.why: The dua ends: 'Anta Mawlana fansurna alal-qawmil-kafirin' — 'You are our Master (and Helper), so help us against the disbelieving people.'

mcqs.q: Which three things do we ask for in the words 'Wa'fu anna, waghfir lana, warhamna'?
mcqs.why: These three words of the dua ask Allah for pardon (wa'fu anna), forgiveness of sins (waghfir lana) and mercy (warhamna) — all three are begged from Allah in this one verse.

mcqs.q: What does the book's lesson summary say about these duas?
options: They are only read in Ramadan
They must be memorized with translation
mcqs.why: The summary printed at the end of the chapter says: the duas told in the Holy Quran in this lesson are necessary to memorize along with their translation.

mcqs.q: How many Quranic duas are given in this 'Hifz and Translation' part?
mcqs.why: The book's page for Hifz and Translation carries exactly two numbered duas: the dua of Al-Baqarah 286 and the dua of Ta-Ha 25–28.

lessons.title: Faith in the Messengers (Risalat and its Requirements)
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Risalat and Nubuwwat

The literal meaning of Risalat is "conveying the message". Rasool means "one who conveys the message". Another word used for Rasool is Nabi, whose literal meaning is "one who gives news". In technical terms, a Rasool and a Nabi is that beloved servant of Allah whom Allah sends with His message for the guidance of humanity.

Khatm-e-Nubuwwat (Finality of Prophethood)

  • The chain of Risalat and Nubuwwat has been ended forever with the Holy Prophet ﷺ.
  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ was sent for the whole world until the Day of Judgement.
  • This belief is called the belief in the Finality of Prophethood (Khatm-e-Nubuwwat).
  • Believing in this creed is absolutely necessary for every Muslim; without accepting it, no person can be a Muslim.

Disrespect of the Messenger

Speaking or writing bad words about the honour of any Prophet, or making a picture of them, is disrespect of the Messenger. In the light of Surah Al-Hujurat, disrespecting the Messenger of Allah ﷺ destroys a person's good deeds, and Allah becomes displeased.

The four requirements of Risalat

  • 1. Love for the Messenger ﷺ
  • 2. Honour and respect
  • 3. Helping him
  • 4. Obedience and following him

A verse about Risalat

"And there is no community at all in which a warner did not pass." (Surah Al-Fatir: 24) — a Nabi and Rasool was sent to every nation. In the Holy Quran, only some Prophets and Messengers are mentioned by name.

Quick points

  • After Allah, the obedience of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is foremost of all.
  • Hazrat Adam (AS) was sent first of all as a Prophet; the Holy Prophet ﷺ was sent last of all, for the whole universe.
  • True love for the Messenger ﷺ makes a person follow him as a practical model.

mcqs.q: What is the literal meaning of 'Risalat'?
mcqs.why: Risalat literally means 'conveying the message'. A Rasool is the one who conveys Allah's message, and a Nabi is the one who gives news — both are Allah's chosen servants sent for the guidance of humanity.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'Nabi' literally mean?
mcqs.why: The book explains both words: Rasool means 'one who conveys the message', while Nabi means 'one who gives news'. Both titles belong to the servant whom Allah sends with His message.

mcqs.q: The belief that the chain of Prophethood ended forever with the Holy Prophet ﷺ is called:
mcqs.why: This belief is called the belief in the Finality of Prophethood — Khatm-e-Nubuwwat. The Holy Prophet ﷺ was sent for the whole world until the Day of Judgement, and accepting this belief is necessary for every Muslim.

mcqs.q: How many requirements of Risalat are there?
mcqs.why: There are four requirements of Risalat: (1) love for the Messenger ﷺ, (2) honour and respect, (3) helping him, and (4) obedience and following him.

mcqs.q: Which of these is NOT a requirement of Risalat?
mcqs.why: The four requirements listed in the lesson are love, honour and respect, helping the Messenger ﷺ, and obedience and following. Wealth and fame are never a requirement of believing in the Messenger.

mcqs.q: What happens to a person's good deeds if he disrespects the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?
mcqs.why: In the light of Surah Al-Hujurat, disrespecting the Messenger of Allah ﷺ destroys a person's good deeds and Allah becomes displeased. Speaking bad words about any Prophet or making his picture is disrespect.

mcqs.q: After Allah, whose obedience is foremost of all?
mcqs.why: The lesson's fill-in answer is clear: after Allah, the obedience of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is foremost of all. Obeying him is itself one of the four requirements of Risalat.

mcqs.q: In the Holy Quran, how many Prophets and Messengers are mentioned by name?
mcqs.why: The lesson states that in the Holy Quran only some Prophets and Messengers are mentioned. A Nabi and Rasool was sent to every nation, but not all of them are named in the Quran.

mcqs.q: Who was sent first of all as a Prophet?
mcqs.why: From the lesson's matching exercise: Hazrat Adam (AS) was sent first of all as a Prophet, while the Holy Prophet ﷺ was sent last of all as a Messenger for the whole universe.

mcqs.q: According to Surah Al-Fatir (verse 24), quoted in this lesson, in every community there passed a:
mcqs.why: The verse says: 'And there is no community at all in which a warner did not pass.' This proves that Allah sent a Nabi and Rasool to every nation for its guidance.

lessons.title: The Concept of Worship in Islam
lessons.notes_html:
Literal meaning of Ibadat

Ibadat (worship) means servitude or slavery — that is, serving one's true Creator and Master, Allah. The person who adopts servitude is called an 'Abd (servant).

The concept of worship in Islam

  • The concept of worship in Islam is very broad and comprehensive.
  • It is NOT limited to Salah, fasting, Zakat, Hajj and Dhikr.
  • All matters of life done according to the command of Allah are also included in worship.
  • Earning lawful (halal) sustenance is itself worship.
  • Doing business according to the teachings of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ is worship.
  • Getting education to serve the country and nation is worship.
  • Not violating the teachings of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ in all matters is called worship.

Purpose of human creation

Allah created the jinn and mankind only for His worship: "And I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they worship Me." (Surah Adh-Dhariyat: 56)

Who benefits from our worship?

The benefit of our worship reaches us alone; it does not reach our Lord. Man can go astray without the servitude of Allah, so Allah has commanded man to worship — for man's own good.

mcqs.q: What is the literal meaning of 'Ibadat'?
mcqs.why: This is the book's own exercise answer: Ibadat means servitude or slavery — serving one's true Creator and Master, Allah. Salah, fasting and Hajj are forms of worship, not its literal meaning.

mcqs.q: In Islam, the concept of worship is:
mcqs.why: The lesson teaches that the concept of worship in Islam is very broad and comprehensive. It is not limited to Salah, fasting, Zakat, Hajj and Dhikr; every matter of life done by Allah's command is worship.

mcqs.q: Why did Allah create the jinn and mankind?
mcqs.why: Allah says in Surah Adh-Dhariyat (56): 'And I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they worship Me.' Worship is the very purpose of our creation.

mcqs.q: Who benefits from our worship?
mcqs.why: The benefit of our worship reaches us alone; it does not reach our Lord. Allah commanded worship because without His servitude man goes astray — so worship is for our own benefit.

mcqs.q: Earning lawful (halal) sustenance is:
mcqs.why: Because the concept of worship is so broad, earning lawful sustenance is itself worship. In the same way, honest business and education for serving the nation are also worship when done by Allah's teachings.

mcqs.q: The person who adopts servitude of Allah is called:
mcqs.why: The book's exercise answer: the one who adopts servitude or slavery (of Allah) is called an 'Abd' — a servant. Ma'bood, by contrast, is the One who is worshipped, i.e. Allah.

mcqs.q: Which of the following did we commonly think worship is limited to?
options: Salah, fasting, Zakat, Hajj and Dhikr
mcqs.why: The lesson corrects our narrow thinking: we understand worship to be only Salah, fasting, Zakat, Hajj and Dhikr, but in Islam every life-matter done according to Allah's command is included in worship.

mcqs.q: Doing business according to the teachings of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ is:
mcqs.why: The lesson marks this statement True: doing business according to the teachings of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ is worship, because worship covers all matters of life done by Allah's command.

mcqs.q: Getting education to serve the country and nation is:
mcqs.why: This is another True statement of the lesson. Education gained to serve the country and nation is worship, since every good act of life done by Allah's command counts as worship.

mcqs.q: Not violating the teachings of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ in all matters is called:
mcqs.why: The book's own MCQ answer: not violating the teachings of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ in all matters is called worship. This shows how wide the Islamic concept of worship is.

lessons.title: Importance and Virtue of Dua
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Dua

Dua is an Arabic word. Its literal meaning is calling or invoking. In Dua, a person calls upon Allah with his tongue or his heart — that is why it is called "Dua".

Why make Dua?

  • Dua is an important act of worship; Dua is the soul of worship.
  • Allah says: "Ask Me in Dua, and I will accept your Dua."
  • In daily life, a person often feels helpless and powerless; when all worldly means fail, man turns to the Being in whose power and wisdom he has complete faith.
  • The noble Prophets used to call upon Allah in every condition.
  • In difficulty, Dua is a precious support for man.

Three forms of acceptance of Dua

  • 1. The Dua is accepted in this world.
  • 2. Or its reward is given in the Hereafter.
  • 3. Or, in place of that Dua, some calamity is averted from the servant.

From whom should Dua be asked?

Dua should be asked from Allah alone. Dua is pure worship, so no one else should be associated with Allah in this act.

Virtues of Dua

  • Dua manifests man's humility (it does NOT show arrogance).
  • Dua is an effective weapon for ending worries.
  • Dua is a means of relief from illnesses and of healing.
  • Dua strengthens the connection with Allah and firms up willpower.
  • Dua increases certainty in the heart and mind, and increases trust in Allah's power.
  • The favourite Dua of the Holy Prophet ﷺ mentioned in the lesson was about knowledge: "Rabbi zidni 'ilma" — "My Lord! Increase me in knowledge."

mcqs.q: Of which language is the word 'Dua', and what does it mean?
mcqs.why: Dua is an Arabic word whose literal meaning is calling or invoking. In Dua a person calls upon Allah with his tongue or his heart, and that is why it is called Dua.

mcqs.q: Dua is called the ______ of worship.
mcqs.why: The lesson says: Dua is an important act of worship; Dua is the soul of worship. Allah Himself says: 'Ask Me in Dua, and I will accept your Dua.'

mcqs.q: How many forms of acceptance of Dua are there?
mcqs.why: There are three forms: (1) the Dua is accepted in this world, (2) its reward is given in the Hereafter, or (3) in place of it, some calamity is averted from the servant. So no Dua of a believer is wasted.

mcqs.q: From whom should Dua be asked?
mcqs.why: According to Islamic teachings, Dua is pure worship, so it should be asked from Allah alone. In this act, no one else should be associated with Allah.

mcqs.q: Which quality does Dua show in a person?
mcqs.why: Dua manifests man's humility — the lesson's true/false section marks 'Dua manifests arrogance' as False. By Dua, a servant admits his helplessness before Allah's power.

mcqs.q: The favourite Dua of the Holy Prophet ﷺ mentioned in the lesson is about:
mcqs.why: The book's exercise answer is 'about knowledge'. The matching exercise gives that Dua: 'Rabbi zidni ilma' — 'My Lord! Increase me in knowledge.'

mcqs.q: Dua is an effective weapon for ending:
mcqs.why: Among the virtues of Dua, the lesson lists: it is an effective weapon for ending worries, a means of relief from illnesses and healing, and it strengthens the connection with Allah.

mcqs.q: In difficulty and helplessness, Dua is for man a precious:
mcqs.why: The lesson's fill-in answer: in difficulty, Dua is a precious support for man. When all material supports and worldly means fail, man turns to Allah, in whose power and wisdom he has complete faith.

mcqs.q: What does Dua do to a person's willpower and certainty?
mcqs.why: The lesson says Dua strengthens and firms up willpower, increases the state of certainty in the heart and mind, and increases trust and reliance on the power and might of Allah.

mcqs.q: The noble Prophets used to call upon Allah:
mcqs.why: The lesson's fill-in answer: the noble Prophets used to call upon that Being (Allah) in every condition. Dua is not only for times of trouble; it is pure worship for every state.

lessons.title: Zakat (Virtue and Social Importance)
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Zakat

The literal meaning of Zakat is purity and increase. Its technical meaning is: to spend wealth in the way of Allah at a fixed rate on a fixed Nisab of wealth. Among financial acts of worship, Zakat has the greatest virtue. Zakat is the right of the poor and the needy, and it is obligatory only on a Muslim who owns the Nisab.

Nisab of Zakat

  • Seven and a half (7½) tolas of gold, or
  • Fifty-two and a half (52½) tolas of silver, or
  • An equal amount of money or trade goods,
  • besides one's basic needs, remaining with him for a full year — then Zakat becomes obligatory on him.

Eight heads of Zakat expenditure

  • 1. The poor (Fuqara)
  • 2. The needy (Masakin)
  • 3. Those who collect Zakat (Amileen)
  • 4. Those whose hearts are to be reconciled to Islam (Mu'allafatul-Quloob)
  • 5. Freeing slaves
  • 6. Debtors
  • 7. Those who strive in the way of Allah
  • 8. Travellers

Social benefits of Zakat

  • Poverty can be removed from society, and the country and nation can progress.
  • It frees a person from destructive moral diseases like miserliness, greed, selfishness and quarrels.
  • Peace and tranquillity come in society, and brotherhood and love are strengthened.
  • Not paying Zakat creates class tension; the Islamic government can take legal action against those who do not pay Zakat.

mcqs.q: What is the literal meaning of 'Zakat'?
mcqs.why: The literal meaning of Zakat is purity and increase: giving Zakat purifies wealth and increases it. Technically, it is to spend wealth in Allah's way at a fixed rate on a fixed Nisab.

mcqs.q: How many heads (masarif) of Zakat expenditure are there?
mcqs.why: There are eight heads of Zakat expenditure: the poor, the needy, Zakat collectors, those whose hearts are reconciled, freeing slaves, debtors, those striving in Allah's way, and travellers.

mcqs.q: The Nisab of gold for Zakat is:
mcqs.why: The Nisab is seven and a half tolas of gold or fifty-two and a half tolas of silver (or equal money or trade goods), besides basic needs, kept for a full year. 'Ten tolas of gold' is marked False in the lesson.

mcqs.q: The Nisab of silver for Zakat is:
mcqs.why: Fifty-two and a half tolas of silver is the Nisab of silver. Seven and a half tolas is the Nisab of gold — the two numbers must not be mixed up.

mcqs.q: For how long must the Nisab wealth remain with a person for Zakat to become obligatory?
mcqs.why: Zakat becomes obligatory when the Nisab amount, besides basic needs, remains with a Muslim for a full year. Then he pays Zakat according to the account of the coming year.

mcqs.q: 'Amileen' in the heads of Zakat means:
mcqs.why: The eight heads include the Amileen — those who collect Zakat (the workers of Zakat). Zakat is the right of the poor, the needy and also of these workers.

mcqs.q: Which moral diseases does paying Zakat cure?
mcqs.why: The lesson lists the destructive moral diseases that Zakat removes: miserliness, greed, selfishness and quarrels. Paying Zakat gives relief from diseases like miserliness and greed.

mcqs.q: Among financial acts of worship, which has the greatest virtue?
mcqs.why: The lesson's fill-in answer: among financial acts of worship, Zakat has the greatest virtue. It is also the right of fellow human beings — the right of the poor and needy upon the rich.

mcqs.q: Legal action against those who do not pay Zakat can be taken by:
mcqs.why: The lesson states that legal action can be taken against those who do not pay Zakat by the Islamic government. Zakat is not just private charity; it is an organized system.

mcqs.q: What does NOT paying Zakat create in society?
mcqs.why: The fill-in answer of the lesson: not paying Zakat creates class tension. By acting on Zakat, poverty can be removed and our country can walk further on the path of progress.

lessons.title: Conquest of Makkah
lessons.notes_html:
Cause of the Conquest of Makkah

Under the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, any tribe could become an ally of the Muslims or of the Quraysh. Banu Khuza'a became allies of the Muslims, and Banu Bakr became allies of the Quraysh. Banu Bakr suddenly attacked Banu Khuza'a at night and killed several of their men even inside the Haram of the Kaaba. In this way the Quraysh broke the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, which became the cause of the Conquest of Makkah.

The three conditions placed before the Quraysh

  • 1. Blood money for the murdered men of Banu Khuza'a must be paid.
  • 2. The Quraysh of Makkah must withdraw their support from the Banu Bakr tribe.
  • 3. Or the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah must be ended.

The march and the conquest

  • The Prophet ﷺ set out towards Makkah Mukarramah with an army of ten thousand Companions in 8 Hijri.
  • The army entered Makkah from all four sides, without shedding blood.
  • Abu Sufyan became Muslim with the encouragement of Hazrat Abbas (RA).
  • The Conquest of Makkah is an unparalleled conquest in the history of the world: "Truth has come and falsehood has perished."

The general amnesty

After the conquest, the Prophet ﷺ granted the Quraysh a general amnesty and said: "Today there is no blame on you; go, you are all free."

  • Whoever took refuge in Abu Sufyan's house was forgiven.
  • Whoever closed the door of his own house was also left alone.
  • Whoever took refuge in the Kaaba was also forgiven.

mcqs.q: Which tribe became the ally of the Muslims under the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah?
mcqs.why: Banu Khuza'a made the Muslims its ally, while the Quraysh made Banu Bakr its ally. When Banu Bakr attacked Banu Khuza'a at night, the treaty was broken.

mcqs.q: Which tribe did the Quraysh of Makkah make their ally?
mcqs.why: The Quraysh made the Banu Bakr tribe their ally. Banu Bakr's night attack on Banu Khuza'a — killing men even inside the Haram of the Kaaba — broke the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.

mcqs.q: In which Hijri year did the Conquest of Makkah take place?
mcqs.why: The Prophet ﷺ set out towards Makkah Mukarramah with an army of ten thousand Companions in 8 Hijri, and Makkah was conquered in the same year.

mcqs.q: How many Companions were in the army at the Conquest of Makkah?
mcqs.why: The army numbered ten thousand Companions. It entered Makkah from all four sides, as the Prophet ﷺ had ordered, and the city was conquered without shedding blood.

mcqs.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ say to the Quraysh after the conquest?
options: 'Today there is no blame on you; go, you are all free'
mcqs.why: Instead of revenge, the Prophet ﷺ granted a general amnesty: 'Today there is no blame on you; go, you are all free.' This is why this conquest is called unparalleled in world history.

mcqs.q: Whoever took refuge in whose house was forgiven?
mcqs.why: The announcement was: whoever takes refuge in Abu Sufyan's house will be forgiven. 'Hazrat Abbas's house' is marked False in the lesson; Hazrat Abbas (RA) had encouraged Abu Sufyan to accept Islam.

mcqs.q: Whoever closed the door of his own house was:
mcqs.why: The lesson marks 'whoever closes the door of his house will be killed' as False. In fact, such a person was left alone — the conquest was bloodless and safe for everyone who stayed peaceful.

mcqs.q: What was one of the three conditions placed before the Quraysh?
options: Pay the blood money of Banu Khuza'a's murdered men
mcqs.why: The three conditions were: (1) blood money for the murdered men of Banu Khuza'a must be paid, (2) the Quraysh must withdraw support from Banu Bakr, or (3) the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah must be ended.

mcqs.q: Who encouraged Abu Sufyan to become Muslim?
mcqs.why: The lesson marks this True: Abu Sufyan became Muslim with the encouragement of Hazrat Abbas (RA), the uncle of the Prophet ﷺ.

mcqs.q: How did the Muslim army enter Makkah?
mcqs.why: The Prophet ﷺ ordered the army to enter Makkah Mukarramah from all four sides. The great Muslim army entered without shedding blood, and truth came while falsehood perished.

lessons.title: Ghazwa Hunain
lessons.notes_html:
Background

After the Conquest of Makkah, the warrior tribes of Banu Hawazin and Banu Thaqif began war preparations. When the Prophet ﷺ learned of this, he sent Hazrat Abdullah bin Abi Hadrad (RA) for investigation. These tribes pitched their tents in Wadi Awtas near Hunain. Hunain is located between Makkah Mukarramah and Taif.

The Muslim army

  • The number of Muslims in the Battle of Hunain was twelve thousand: ten thousand who had been with the Prophet ﷺ at the Conquest of Makkah, and two thousand new Muslims who also joined.
  • The battle took place in 8 Hijri.
  • The disbelievers' army suddenly showered a rain of arrows upon the Muslims, and the Muslims faced a temporary setback.

Why Allah's help was delayed

The thought came into the Muslims' hearts that since they were greater in number, they would certainly win. Such reliance on numbers was against trust and reliance on Allah, so for a while the Muslims were deprived of Allah's help. The Prophet ﷺ stood firm and called out: "I am the Prophet, and this is not falsehood; I am the son of Abdul Muttalib."

Treatment of the prisoners

On the request of Banu Hawazin, the Prophet ﷺ freed the prisoners of his share, and following his example, the Companions (RA) also freed the prisoners of their shares. Much booty also came into the Muslims' hands.

The lesson of Hunain

Allah's help does not depend on numbers, but on trust in Allah, patience and steadfastness. Relying on oneself instead of Allah's help is never pleasing to Allah.

mcqs.q: The Battle of Hunain was fought against which tribes?
mcqs.why: This is the book's own exercise question: the Battle of Hunain was fought against Banu Hawazin and Banu Thaqif, the warrior tribes who were preparing for war after the Conquest of Makkah.

mcqs.q: What was the number of Muslims in the Battle of Hunain?
mcqs.why: The number was twelve thousand: ten thousand was the army present at the Conquest of Makkah, and two thousand new Muslims also joined this army.

mcqs.q: In which year did the Battle of Hunain take place?
mcqs.why: The Battle of Hunain took place in 8 Hijri, soon after the Conquest of Makkah in the same year.

mcqs.q: Which Companion did the Prophet ﷺ send to investigate the enemy's war preparations?
mcqs.why: When the Prophet ﷺ learned of the war preparations of the warrior tribes, he sent Hazrat Abdullah bin Abi Hadrad (RA) for investigation.

mcqs.q: Hunain is located:
mcqs.why: The book's exercise answer: Hunain is located between Makkah Mukarramah and Taif. Banu Hawazin and Banu Thaqif pitched their tents in Wadi Awtas near Hunain.

mcqs.q: In which valley did Banu Hawazin and Banu Thaqif pitch their tents?
mcqs.why: The fill-in answer of the lesson: the tribes pitched their tents in Wadi Awtas near Hunain. 'Near Hunain is Wadi Abu Talib' is marked False.

mcqs.q: Why were the Muslims deprived of Allah's help for a while at Hunain?
options: They relied on their large number instead of Allah
mcqs.why: The thought that 'we are greater in number, so we will certainly win' was against trust and reliance on Allah. Such self-reliance displeased Allah, so His help was withheld for a while.

mcqs.q: At Hunain, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'I am the Prophet, and this is not falsehood; I am the ______ of Abdul Muttalib.'
mcqs.why: Standing firm in the battle, the Prophet ﷺ called out: 'I am the Prophet, and this is not falsehood; I am the son of Abdul Muttalib' — reminding the Muslims of his steadfastness.

mcqs.q: How did the Prophet ﷺ treat the prisoners of Banu Hawazin?
options: He freed the prisoners of his share
mcqs.why: On the request of Banu Hawazin, the Prophet ﷺ freed the prisoners of his share, and following his example, the Companions (RA) also freed the prisoners of their shares.

mcqs.q: What is the great lesson of the Battle of Hunain?
options: Allah's help depends on trust in Him, patience and steadfastness
mcqs.why: The lesson of Hunain: Allah's help does not depend on numbers, but on trust in Allah, patience and steadfastness. Relying on oneself instead of Allah is never pleasing to Him.

lessons.title: Ghazwa Tabuk
lessons.notes_html:
Background

Tabuk is located at a distance of about 500 kilometres from Madinah Munawwarah. In the Battle of Tabuk, the Muslims faced the army of Heraclius, the king of Rome — who had become afraid of the growing power of the Muslims — although no battle took place. The expedition took place in 9 Hijri.

The army and the hard journey

  • The number of Muslims in this battle was thirty thousand.
  • The great Muslim army reached the field of Tabuk after about fourteen days.
  • Because of the severe heat on the way, the army's animals became tired. The Quran described this severe trial and difficult conditions as 'usrat' (hardship).
  • The Prophet ﷺ appointed Hazrat Ali (RA) as his deputy in Madinah Munawwarah.

Financial sacrifices

  • Hazrat Usman Ghani (RA) presented one hundred camels, one thousand horses, one hundred uqiyah of silver and one thousand dinars in the way of Allah.
  • Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA) brought all the goods of his house to the service of the Prophet ﷺ.
  • Hazrat Umar Farooq (RA) presented half of his household goods.
  • Hazrat Abu Aqeel (RA), by labouring, presented half the dates (a small amount earned by work) in the service of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Why no battle took place

The awe of the Muslims' courage and bravery fell upon the Christians so much that they abandoned the very intention of fighting. The Muslims waited for the Christians for twenty days, then returned without a battle. With Tabuk, the Muslims' morale became even stronger.

mcqs.q: Tabuk is located at about what distance from Madinah Munawwarah?
mcqs.why: The book's exercise answer: the region of Tabuk is far from Madinah Munawwarah by five hundred kilometres. The statement 'about 400 kilometres' is marked False in the lesson.

mcqs.q: In the Battle of Tabuk, the Muslims faced the army of:
mcqs.why: The Muslims faced the army of Heraclius, the king of Rome, who had become afraid of the growing power of the Muslims — although in the end no battle took place.

mcqs.q: What was the number of Muslims in the Battle of Tabuk?
mcqs.why: The number of Muslims in this battle was thirty thousand — the largest army of the Prophet's ﷺ expeditions in this book.

mcqs.q: In which Hijri year did the Battle of Tabuk take place?
mcqs.why: The lesson marks this True: the Battle of Tabuk took place in 9 Hijri.

mcqs.q: Why did no battle take place at Tabuk?
options: The awe of the Muslims' bravery made the Christians abandon fighting
mcqs.why: The awe of the Muslims' courage and bravery fell upon the Christians so much that they abandoned the very intention of fighting. The claim 'the Muslims were defeated at Tabuk' is False — there was no battle at all.

mcqs.q: For how many days did the Muslims wait for the Christians at Tabuk?
mcqs.why: The Muslims waited for the Christians for twenty days, then returned without a battle. (Fourteen days was the length of the journey to reach Tabuk.)

mcqs.q: Whom did the Prophet ﷺ appoint as deputy in Madinah during Tabuk?
mcqs.why: On the occasion of the Battle of Tabuk, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed Hazrat Ali (RA) as deputy in Madinah Munawwarah.

mcqs.q: What did Hazrat Usman Ghani (RA) present for the Tabuk expedition?
options: One hundred camels, one thousand horses, silver and one thousand dinars
mcqs.why: Hazrat Usman Ghani (RA) presented one hundred camels, one thousand horses, one hundred uqiyah of silver and one thousand dinars in the way of Allah — a famous financial sacrifice.

mcqs.q: What did Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA) bring for this expedition?
options: All the goods of his house
mcqs.why: Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA) brought all the goods of his house to the service of the Prophet ﷺ. Hazrat Umar Farooq (RA) presented half of his household goods.

mcqs.q: The Quran described the severe trial and difficult conditions of Tabuk as 'usrat', which means:
mcqs.why: 'Usrat' means hardship. The journey was made in severe heat, the army's animals became tired, and this expedition is remembered as the army of hardship (Jaish-ul-Usrat).

lessons.title: Khutba Hajjat-ul-Wida (The Farewell Sermon)
lessons.notes_html:
Why "Hijjat-ul-Wida"?

It was the last Hajj of the Prophet ﷺ, which is why it is called Hijjat-ul-Wida (the Farewell Hajj). The Prophet ﷺ had said: "Listen to my words attentively; it may be that after this year I may not meet you here again." Hijjat-ul-Wida took place in 10 Hijri.

The journey

  • On 8 Dhul-Hijjah, the Prophet ﷺ came to Mina.
  • After offering the Fajr prayer on 9 Dhul-Hijjah, the Prophet ﷺ rode his she-camel Qaswa and came to the field of Arafat, where he delivered the famous sermon.

Teachings of the Farewell Sermon

  • Rights of slaves: "Your slaves have rights over you: whatever you eat yourselves, feed them the same; whatever you wear yourselves, clothe them the same; and help them in the tasks placed upon them."
  • Rights of women: "Fear Allah concerning women. You have rights over women, and women have rights over you."
  • All the interest/usury of the age of ignorance was announced abolished.
  • All Muslims among themselves are brothers; all are servants of Allah and children of Hazrat Adam (AS).
  • Take care of prayer; repay the debt; return a picked-up thing to its owner.

Historical status

The Sermon of Hijjat-ul-Wida is an important charter of human rights in human history — a magnificent charter of human rights.

mcqs.q: Why is this Hajj called 'Hijjat-ul-Wida'?
options: It was the last Hajj of the Prophet ﷺ
mcqs.why: It was the last Hajj of the Prophet ﷺ, so it is called Hijjat-ul-Wida — the Farewell Hajj. He ﷺ said: 'Listen to my words attentively; it may be that after this year I may not meet you here again.'

mcqs.q: In which Hijri year did Hijjat-ul-Wida take place?
mcqs.why: Hijjat-ul-Wida took place in 10 Hijri. The Prophet ﷺ intended to perform Hajj in 10 Hijri, and the sermon was delivered in the same journey.

mcqs.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about the rights of slaves in the Farewell Sermon?
options: Feed them what you eat and clothe them what you wear
Slaves should work day and night
mcqs.why: He ﷺ said: 'Your slaves have rights over you: whatever you eat yourselves, feed them the same; whatever you wear yourselves, clothe them the same; and help them in the tasks placed upon them.'

mcqs.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ say concerning women in the sermon?
options: Fear Allah concerning women; you have rights over them and they have rights over you
mcqs.why: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Fear Allah concerning women. You have rights over women, and women have rights over you.' The sermon protects the rights of both sides.

mcqs.q: The Sermon of Hijjat-ul-Wida is a magnificent ______ of human rights.
mcqs.why: The lesson calls the Sermon of Hijjat-ul-Wida an important and magnificent charter of human rights in human history — the first great declaration of the rights of mankind.

mcqs.q: On 8 Dhul-Hijjah, the Prophet ﷺ came to:
mcqs.why: On 8 Dhul-Hijjah the Prophet ﷺ came to Mina. Then, after the Fajr prayer of 9 Dhul-Hijjah, he rode to the field of Arafat.

mcqs.q: After Fajr on 9 Dhul-Hijjah, the Prophet ﷺ came to the field of Arafat riding his she-camel named:
mcqs.why: The lesson's fill-in answer: he rode his she-camel Qaswa and came to the field of Arafat, where the blessed rite of Hajj is performed on 9 Dhul-Hijjah.

mcqs.q: Which practice of the age of ignorance did the Prophet ﷺ announce as abolished in the sermon?
mcqs.why: The Prophet ﷺ said that all the interest/usury of the age of ignorance has been abolished. ('Do not repay the debt' is False — the sermon teaches repaying debts and returning trusts.)

mcqs.q: According to the sermon's matching exercise, a picked-up thing should be:
mcqs.why: The sermon teaches trustworthiness: repay the debt, and return the picked-up thing to its owner. All Muslims are brothers among themselves and children of Hazrat Adam (AS).

mcqs.q: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Listen to my words attentively; it may be that ______ I may not meet you here again.'
mcqs.why: These words show why the Hajj is called 'farewell': 'It may be that after this year I may not meet you here again.' The Prophet ﷺ passed away the next year, in 11 Hijri.

lessons.title: Wisal (Demise of the Holy Prophet ﷺ)
lessons.notes_html:
Purpose of the Prophet's ﷺ advent

The purpose of the Prophet's ﷺ advent (bi'that) was to end disbelief and polytheism and to establish the religion of Allah in practice. By the time of his passing, the religion had prevailed over the whole of Arabia, and his blessed age was sixty-three years.

The illness

  • On the last day of the month of Safar, the Prophet ﷺ went to the Jannat-ul-Baqi (Baqi-ul-Gharqad) graveyard; after that he fell ill.
  • During the days of his severe illness, Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA) led the prayer as Imam — the Prophet ﷺ himself ordered Bibi Aisha (RA) to instruct Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) to lead the prayer.
  • Coming to the mosque in his illness, he said: "Allah has given a servant the choice to accept the blessings of the world or what is with Allah, but that servant has chosen what is with Allah."
  • The Prophet ﷺ came to the mosque leaning on the shoulders of two Companions (not Hazrat Hamza (RA), who had been martyred earlier).

The Wisal

  • The Wisal took place in 11 Hijri, on Monday, 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal, at Chasht (mid-morning) time.
  • After using the miswak at the time of Wisal, he said: "With those Prophets, truthful ones, martyrs and righteous ones whom You have blessed. O Allah! Forgive me, have mercy on me and join me to the Highest Companion. O Allah! The Highest Companion."
  • Hazrat Umar (RA), in the emotion of love, said that whoever says the Prophet ﷺ has passed away, he would cut off his hands and feet — many Companions could not believe the news.
  • The Prophet ﷺ was buried in the chamber of Bibi Aisha (RA).

mcqs.q: What was the purpose of the Prophet's ﷺ advent (bi'that)?
options: To end disbelief and polytheism and establish Allah's religion
mcqs.why: The purpose of his advent was to end disbelief and polytheism and to establish the religion of Allah in practice. By his Wisal, the religion had prevailed over the whole of Arabia.

mcqs.q: Who led the prayer as Imam during the Prophet's ﷺ severe illness?
mcqs.why: Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA) led the prayer as Imam for several days during the Prophet's ﷺ illness — by the Prophet's ﷺ own order, given through Bibi Aisha (RA).

mcqs.q: In which Hijri year did the Prophet's ﷺ Wisal take place?
mcqs.why: The Wisal took place in 11 Hijri, on Monday, 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal, at Chasht (mid-morning) time.

mcqs.q: On which date and day did the Wisal occur?
mcqs.why: The lesson marks this True: the Prophet's ﷺ Wisal took place at Chasht time on 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal, 11 Hijri, and that day was Monday.

mcqs.q: At what time of day did the Wisal take place?
mcqs.why: The fill-in answer of the lesson: the Wisal of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took place at Chasht time — the mid-morning.

mcqs.q: On the last day of Safar, the Prophet ﷺ went to which graveyard?
mcqs.why: On the last day of the month of Safar, the Prophet ﷺ went to the Jannat-ul-Baqi graveyard in Madinah; from there his illness began.

mcqs.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ say in the mosque during his illness?
options: 'A servant has chosen what is with Allah over the blessings of the world'
mcqs.why: He ﷺ said: 'Allah has given a servant the choice to accept the blessings of the world or what is with Allah, but that servant has chosen what is with Allah.' Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) understood he meant himself.

mcqs.q: After using the miswak at the time of Wisal, the Prophet ﷺ prayed for:
options: Being joined to the Highest Companion
mcqs.why: His last words were: 'O Allah! Forgive me, have mercy on me and join me to the Highest Companion. O Allah! The Highest Companion.'

mcqs.q: Where was the Prophet ﷺ buried?
options: In the chamber of Bibi Aisha (RA)
mcqs.why: After the Wisal, the Prophet ﷺ was buried in the chamber (hujrah) of Bibi Aisha (RA) — the very room where he passed away.

mcqs.q: What was the blessed age of the Prophet ﷺ at the time of Wisal?
mcqs.why: The matching exercise of the lesson gives: at the time of Wisal, the Prophet's ﷺ blessed age was sixty-three years.

lessons.title: Virtue of Generosity and Condemnation of Miserliness
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning and concept of generosity (Sakhawat)

Generosity means fulfilling the needs of the needy for the pleasure of Allah Almighty. Its concept is not limited to financial sacrifice alone; benefiting others through every kind of one's abilities is also generosity. One who, despite having means, does not spend on his own and the needy's lawful needs is called a miser.

Benefits of generosity

  • Generosity earns the love and pleasure of Allah Almighty — Allah Almighty loves the generous person.
  • Generosity brings peace and contentment to the heart.
  • Hadith: "A generous person is near to Allah Almighty, near to Paradise, near to people, and far from Hell."
  • The Quran says: "And they spend (in the way of Allah) from the sustenance We have given them." (Al-Baqarah: 3)
  • Allah Almighty has declared generosity a loan to Himself and a means of purifying the soul.

Condemnation of miserliness

  • Adopting miserliness is ingratitude for Allah Almighty's blessing; it does NOT earn His pleasure.
  • Miserliness is a negative attitude, not a positive one.
  • Generosity has been greatly praised in the Quran and Hadith, and the blessed life of the Holy Prophet ﷺ is a splendid example of generosity — at his passing he left behind no dirham or dinar.
  • Islam teaches that Allah Almighty tests one person by giving more wealth, and gives less wealth to another.

With whom may one compete?

The Holy Prophet ﷺ said one may compete only with two kinds of people: one whom Allah has blessed with wealth and who spends it in the way of Allah, and the other whom Allah has blessed with knowledge and wisdom, who decides according to it and teaches it.

mcqs.q: What does generosity (sakhawat) mean?
options: Fulfilling the needs of the needy for the pleasure of Allah
mcqs.why: Generosity means fulfilling the need of the needy for the pleasure of Allah Almighty. It is not limited to money — benefiting others through every kind of ability is also generosity.

mcqs.q: A person who, despite having means, does not spend on lawful needs is called:
mcqs.why: The lesson's fill-in answer: such a person is called a miser. Miserliness is ingratitude for Allah's blessing and is condemned in Islam.

mcqs.q: According to the hadith in this lesson, a generous person is:
options: Near to Allah, near to Paradise, near to people, far from Hell
mcqs.why: The blessed saying of the Holy Prophet ﷺ is: 'A generous person is near to Allah Almighty, near to Paradise, near to people, and far from Hell.'

mcqs.q: Which are two benefits of generosity named in the lesson?
options: Allah's love and pleasure, and peace of the heart
mcqs.why: The lesson answers: generosity earns the love and pleasure of Allah Almighty, and generosity brings peace and contentment to the heart.

mcqs.q: Allah Almighty loves:
mcqs.why: The fill-in answer is 'the generous person', and the true/false section confirms: 'Allah Almighty loves the generous person' is True, while 'miserliness earns Allah's pleasure' is False.

mcqs.q: Adopting miserliness is ______ for Allah Almighty's blessing.
mcqs.why: The lesson states in one line: adopting miserliness is ingratitude for the blessing of Allah Almighty. The generous use of His blessings is true thankfulness.

mcqs.q: With which two kinds of people did the Prophet ﷺ allow competition (rashk)?
options: One who spends his wealth in Allah's way, and one who acts on and teaches his knowledge
mcqs.why: One may compete only with: (1) a person blessed with wealth who spends it in the way of Allah, and (2) a person blessed with knowledge and wisdom who decides according to it and teaches it.

mcqs.q: At the time of his passing, the Holy Prophet ﷺ left behind:
mcqs.why: From the matching exercise: at the time of his passing, the Holy Prophet ﷺ left behind no dirham or dinar. His blessed life is a splendid example of generosity.

mcqs.q: Allah Almighty has declared generosity, upon Himself, as:
mcqs.why: The matching exercise says Allah Almighty has declared generosity upon Himself as a loan, and declared generosity a means of purifying the soul — so what is spent for Him is never lost.

mcqs.q: According to the lesson, why does Allah give more wealth to one person and less to another?
mcqs.why: Islam teaches that Allah Almighty tests one by giving more wealth, and gives less wealth to another. The test is passed by generosity, not by hoarding.

lessons.title: Miana Ravi (Moderation)
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Miana Ravi (Moderation)

"Miana ravi" is a Persian word; in Arabic it is called "i'tidal". Its literal meaning is the middle path. Its concept is that in all matters of life, one should avoid excess and negligence and adopt the middle path. Moderation is also called balance.

Three kinds of moderation in this lesson

  • 1. Moderation in religion
  • 2. Moderation in society
  • 3. Moderation in business dealings

Moderation in the Quran and Hadith

  • The Muslim community is named "Ummah Wasat" — the middle, balanced community: "And thus We have made you a balanced community." (Al-Baqarah: 143)
  • The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever adopts moderation will never be needy."
  • The deed most liked by Allah Almighty is the one adopted consistently, even if it is small.
  • The Prophet ﷺ said: "I pray at night and also rest" — in worship too there is balance.
  • Even in walking and speaking, moderation is taught: walk with a moderate pace and use a balanced voice — neither harsh nor too soft.
  • In charity too, neither miserliness nor extravagance should be shown.

Moderation in business dealings

It means that in daily personal or household expenses, one should neither be extravagant nor miserly when spending, but should adopt the middle path. Past nations fell victim to excess and negligence; life with moderation becomes happy and successful.

mcqs.q: 'Miana ravi' is a word of which language?
mcqs.why: The book's own exercise answer: 'Miana ravi' is a Persian word; in Arabic it is called 'i'tidal'. The statement 'Miana ravi is an Arabic word' is False.

mcqs.q: What does 'i'tidal' mean?
mcqs.why: I'tidal means moderation — adopting the middle path in all matters of life, avoiding both excess and negligence. Moderation is also called balance.

mcqs.q: Into how many kinds is moderation divided in this lesson?
mcqs.why: Moderation is divided into three kinds: moderation in religion, moderation in society, and moderation in business dealings. 'Four kinds' is marked False in the lesson.

mcqs.q: In the Holy Quran, 'Ummah Wasat' means:
mcqs.why: Allah says in Al-Baqarah (143): 'And thus We have made you a balanced community.' The Muslim community is named Ummah Wasat — the middle, balanced community.

mcqs.q: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever adopts moderation will never be ______.'
mcqs.why: This is the blessed saying quoted in the lesson about the importance of moderation: whoever adopts moderation (iqtisad) will never be needy.

mcqs.q: Moderation in business dealings means:
options: Neither extravagance nor miserliness in spending
mcqs.why: In daily personal or household expenses, one should neither be extravagant nor miserly when spending, but adopt the middle path. This is the lesson's own explanation of moderation in business dealings (mu'amalat).

mcqs.q: The deed most liked by Allah Almighty is the one:
mcqs.why: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said that the deed most liked by Allah Almighty is the one adopted consistently, even if it is small. The Prophet ﷺ himself prayed at night and also rested.

mcqs.q: In the Holy Quran, Allah commands moderation even in:
mcqs.why: The fill-in answer: Allah Almighty commands to walk with a moderate pace in one's walking. In speaking too, the voice should be balanced — neither harsh nor very soft.

mcqs.q: In charity, what should be avoided?
mcqs.why: From the matching exercise: in charity too, neither miserliness nor extravagance should be shown. Moderation applies to spending for others just as to spending on oneself.

mcqs.q: What happened to the various sectors of past nations?
options: They fell victim to excess and negligence
mcqs.why: The matching exercise states: the various sectors of past nations fell victim to excess and negligence. Life with moderation, by contrast, becomes happy and successful.

lessons.title: Musawat (Equality)
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning and concept of Musawat (Equality)

"Musawat" is an Arabic word meaning equality — treating equally. Its concept is that all human beings share the same origin, so they are equal in the eyes of the law and equal to one another in rights. No one is inferior to another. The standard of greatness and personal nobility is only piety.

Equality in the words of the Prophet ﷺ and the Quran

  • Hadith: "Beware! No Arab has superiority over a non-Arab, nor a non-Arab over an Arab, nor a black person over a white person, nor a white person over a black person, except by piety."
  • Quran: "Indeed, the most honoured of you before Allah is the most righteous among you." (Al-Hujurat: 13) — the standard of superiority is not colour or race, but piety and righteousness.
  • The Prophet ﷺ said that if even the daughter of Muhammad ﷺ, Fatimah, had stolen, her hand would have been cut too — the law is equal for all.
  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ and the Companions were a practical model of equality; through his actions the Prophet ﷺ ended racial discrimination forever.

Examples from the Companions

  • Hazrat Umar (RA) used to call Hazrat Bilal Habshi (RA) "Ya Sayyidi" — "my master".
  • On the journey to Jerusalem for the conquest of Palestine, Hazrat Umar (RA) took turns riding with his slave: sometimes he seated the slave on the mount and sometimes he himself walked on foot.
  • Hazrat Abu Dharr Ghifari (RA) used to dress his slave in the same clothes he wore himself.
  • The Prophet ﷺ made Hazrat Bilal Habshi (RA) the muezzin of Masjid-e-Nabawi, and married his freed slave Hazrat Zaid bin Harithah (RA) to his cousin Hazrat Zainab (RA).

Equality in worship

In prayer, all worshippers stand shoulder to shoulder; in fasting, all fasting people appear in the same condition — Islamic worships are a practical display of equality.

mcqs.q: What does 'musawat' mean?
mcqs.why: 'Musawat' is an Arabic word meaning equality — treating equally. All human beings share the same origin, so they are equal before the law and equal in rights.

mcqs.q: From which language is the word 'musawat'?
mcqs.why: The lesson answers directly: 'Musawat' is an Arabic word. Its concept is that no one is inferior to another; the standard of nobility is only piety.

mcqs.q: According to the Holy Quran, what is the standard of superiority and nobility?
mcqs.why: The Quran says: 'Indeed, the most honoured of you before Allah is the most righteous among you' (Al-Hujurat: 13). The standard is piety and righteousness, not colour or race. 'The standard is not piety' is marked False.

mcqs.q: Hazrat Umar (RA) used to call Hazrat Bilal Habshi (RA):
mcqs.why: Hazrat Umar (RA) used to call Hazrat Bilal Habshi (RA) 'Ya Sayyidi' — 'my master'. This is the lesson's example of equality from the lives of the Companions.

mcqs.q: On the journey to Jerusalem, how did Hazrat Umar (RA) travel with his slave?
options: The slave rode while he ran
He rode while the slave walked
mcqs.why: They took turns riding: sometimes Hazrat Umar (RA) seated the slave on the mount and walked on foot himself, and sometimes he rode. A practical model of equality by the Caliph himself.

mcqs.q: Hazrat Abu Dharr Ghifari (RA) used to dress his slave in:
options: The same clothes he wore himself
mcqs.why: The fill-in answer: Hazrat Abu Dharr Ghifari (RA) used to dress his slave in the same clothes he wore himself — no difference between master and slave in dress.

mcqs.q: The Holy Prophet ﷺ made Hazrat Bilal Habshi (RA) the ______ of Masjid-e-Nabawi.
mcqs.why: The Prophet ﷺ made Hazrat Bilal Habshi (RA) the muezzin of Masjid-e-Nabawi — the one who calls the Azan. Honour in Islam is by piety, not by birth or colour.

mcqs.q: The Prophet ﷺ married his freed slave Hazrat Zaid bin Harithah (RA) to:
mcqs.why: The Prophet ﷺ married Hazrat Zaid bin Harithah (RA), his freed slave, to his own cousin Hazrat Zainab (RA) — breaking the pride of family and status by action.

mcqs.q: If even Fatimah, the daughter of Muhammad ﷺ, had stolen, the Prophet ﷺ said:
options: Her hand would be cut too
mcqs.why: This shows equality before the law: even the Prophet's ﷺ own daughter would receive the same punishment. In Islam the law is equal for the high and the low.

mcqs.q: In prayer, equality is seen because all worshippers:
options: Sit in separate rows by wealth
mcqs.why: From the matching exercise: in prayer, all worshippers stand shoulder to shoulder, and in fasting all appear in the same condition. Reflecting on Islamic worships, a practical display of equality is seen.

lessons.title: Greatness of Hard Work
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning and concept of labour

Labour means enduring hardship and toil. Its concept is that a person works with his own hands to arrange his livelihood and does his own work with his own hands.

Personal and social benefits of labour

  • Personal benefits: Labour creates self-respect in a person. Labour keeps a person active and saves him from illness and laziness. A hardworking person does not stretch out his hand before anyone.
  • Social benefits: Labour brings progress in society and increases prosperity.

Labour in the Quran and Hadith

  • Quran: "Then when the prayer is finished, disperse in the land and seek Allah's bounty (sustenance), and remember Allah much so that you may succeed." (Al-Jumu'ah: 10)
  • Hadith: "The earner is the friend of Allah."
  • The best sustenance of a person is what he earns with his own hands.
  • A labourer's wages should be paid before his sweat dries.
  • The Prophet ﷺ disapproved of begging and said: the upper hand (the giver) is better than the lower hand (the receiver).

Prophets who worked

  • Hazrat Nuh (AS) used to trade.
  • Hazrat Idris (AS) used to do tailoring work.
  • Hazrat Dawud (AS) used to make armour.
  • Hazrat Musa (AS) used to farm.
  • The last Prophet, Hazrat Muhammad ﷺ, also grazed goats.
  • The best people of the world are the Prophets — and they worked with their hands.

mcqs.q: What is the literal meaning of labour?
mcqs.why: Labour means enduring hardship and toil. Its concept: a person works with his own hands to arrange his livelihood and does his own work with his own hands.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a PERSONAL benefit of labour?
options: It creates self-respect in a person
mcqs.why: Personal benefits: labour creates self-respect, keeps a person active, and saves him from illness and laziness. Progress in society and increased prosperity are its social benefits.

mcqs.q: A hardworking person does not:
options: Stretch out his hand before anyone
mcqs.why: The lesson says a hardworking person is saved from stretching out his hand before anyone — he earns his own livelihood and keeps his self-respect.

mcqs.q: According to the Prophet ﷺ, the best sustenance of a person is:
options: What he earns with his own hands
mcqs.why: The Prophet ﷺ taught that the best sustenance is what a person earns with his own hands, and he also called the earner 'the friend of Allah'.

mcqs.q: The Prophet ﷺ said to pay the labourer his wages before:
mcqs.why: The fill-in answer: pay the labourer his wages before his sweat dries. Islam joins the greatness of labour with the rights of the labourer.

mcqs.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ declare about begging?
mcqs.why: The Prophet ﷺ declared begging disliked. He said the upper hand (the giver) is better than the lower hand (the receiver) — earning is honourable, begging is not.

mcqs.q: Hazrat Idris (AS) used to do which work?
mcqs.why: From the lesson's true statements: Hazrat Idris (AS) used to do tailoring work. Hazrat Nuh (AS) traded, Hazrat Dawud (AS) made armour, and Hazrat Musa (AS) farmed.

mcqs.q: Hazrat Dawud (AS) used to:
mcqs.why: Hazrat Dawud (AS) used to make armour with his own hands. ('Hazrat Adam (AS) used to graze goats' is marked False in the lesson — it was the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ who grazed goats.)

mcqs.q: What does the Quran command after the Jumu'ah prayer, as quoted in this lesson?
options: Disperse in the land and seek Allah's bounty
mcqs.why: Al-Jumu'ah (10): 'Then when the prayer is finished, disperse in the land and seek Allah's bounty (sustenance), and remember Allah much so that you may succeed.' Work follows worship.

mcqs.q: What is a SOCIAL benefit of labour?
options: Progress in society and increased prosperity
mcqs.why: The lesson divides the benefits: personal benefits are self-respect, activeness and health; the social benefits are that labour brings progress in society and increases prosperity.

lessons.title: Islamic Teachings on Environmental Pollution
lessons.notes_html:
What is environmental pollution?

The things around a human being are called the environment. When such things enter the environment as are harmful to human health and living beings, it is called environmental pollution.

Three kinds of pollution

  • 1. Air pollution
  • 2. Water pollution
  • 3. Noise pollution

Why does Islam dislike pollution?

  • Islam stresses keeping the environment clean and pure.
  • "And Allah loves those who keep themselves clean." (Al-Tawbah: 108)
  • "And Allah does not like corruption." (Al-Baqarah: 205)
  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ declared planting trees an ongoing charity (sadaqah jariyah).
  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ stressed keeping water and the environment clean, and said: "The best of people is the one who brings benefit to other people."
  • With water pollution, water no longer remains fit for human consumption.

Protecting the air

Planting trees is very useful against air pollution, because trees absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen. Along with this, one should avoid the smoke of factories and vehicles, use vehicles that do not emit smoke, and not burn garbage near residential areas.

Noise pollution

Noise pollution is called noise. Sound beyond limits becomes noise and pollutes the environment. The noise of vehicles, the pressure horns fitted in them, and the unnecessary and loud use of loudspeakers cause noise pollution — so the unnecessary use of loudspeakers should be avoided.

mcqs.q: The things around a human being are called:
mcqs.why: The lesson defines it simply: the things around a human being are called the environment. When harmful things enter it, it becomes environmental pollution.

mcqs.q: How many kinds of environmental pollution are there?
mcqs.why: There are three kinds: air pollution, water pollution and noise pollution.

mcqs.q: Trees protect us from air pollution because they:
options: Absorb oxygen and release carbon dioxide
Absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen
mcqs.why: Trees absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen — 'trees absorb oxygen' is marked False in the lesson. That is why planting trees is very useful against air pollution.

mcqs.q: The Holy Prophet ﷺ declared planting trees as:
mcqs.why: From the matching exercise: the Holy Prophet ﷺ declared planting trees ongoing charity — its reward continues as long as people and animals benefit from the tree.

mcqs.q: Which of these spreads noise pollution?
options: Pressure horns and loud use of loudspeakers
mcqs.why: Noise pollution is caused by the noise of vehicles, the pressure horns fitted in them, and the unnecessary and loud use of loudspeakers. Sound beyond limits becomes noise.

mcqs.q: Near residential areas, we should not burn:
mcqs.why: The lesson's fill-in points: we should not burn garbage near residential areas, should avoid the smoke of factories and vehicles, and should use vehicles that do not emit smoke.

mcqs.q: What happens with water pollution?
options: Water no longer remains fit for human consumption
mcqs.why: The lesson marks this True: with water pollution, water no longer remains fit for human consumption. The Prophet ﷺ stressed keeping water and the environment clean.

mcqs.q: Allah says: 'And Allah loves those who ______.' (Al-Tawbah: 108)
mcqs.why: The verse quoted in the lesson: 'And Allah loves those who keep themselves clean.' And in Al-Baqarah (205): 'Allah does not like corruption.' Cleanliness is part of faith and environment care.

mcqs.q: The Holy Prophet ﷺ said: 'The best of people is the one who brings ______ to other people.'
mcqs.why: The fill-in answer is 'benefit'. Keeping the environment clean is one way of benefiting others; polluting it harms everyone around us.

mcqs.q: Pollution, according to the lesson, is:
options: The basis of life on earth
Harmful to human health and living beings
mcqs.why: 'Pollution is the basis of life on this earth' is marked False. Pollution means harmful things entering the environment, damaging human health and living beings — that is why Islam dislikes it.

lessons.title: Huqooq-ul-Ibad (Relatives, Guests, the Sick)
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Huqooq-ul-Ibad

"Huqooq" is the plural of "haq"; the literal meaning of "haq" is "an established thing and consideration". Huqooq-ul-Ibad means those duties which Allah Almighty has made obligatory upon servants towards one another. One servant's right becomes binding upon another as a duty. There are two kinds of rights: Huqooq-Allah and Huqooq-ul-Ibad. Among human relationships, relatives have the greatest importance.

Rights of relatives

  • To share in their joys and sorrows.
  • To treat them well and help them in difficult times.
  • To avoid causing them any kind of hardship.
  • "And give relatives their right." (Bani Isra'il: 26) — keeping ties joined is commanded, and breaking ties is strictly forbidden; one who breaks ties will not enter Paradise.
  • Practical example: to welcome his foster mother Bibi Halimah Sa'diyah (RA), the Holy Prophet ﷺ would spread his cloak for her, speak to her attentively, and send her off with love and many gifts.

Rights of a guest

  • To honour the guest and serve him as much as possible.
  • To look after the guest's comfort.
  • To make no distinction between Muslim and non-Muslim in these rights; the guest should also look after his host.
  • The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever believes in Allah Almighty and the Last Day should honour his guest." In a good society, the guest is honoured; hospitality is the Sunnah of the Prophets, and the hospitality of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is mentioned in the Holy Quran.

Rights of the sick

  • When someone falls ill, one should visit him, without delay, and pray for his recovery.
  • Give the sick person support and encouragement in his pain, and help him besides treatment, as needed.
  • The Prophet ﷺ would visit the sick without distinguishing between Muslim and non-Muslim — he even visited his enemies. Visiting the sick is pleasing to Allah Almighty.

mcqs.q: 'Huqooq' is the plural of 'haq'. The literal meaning of 'haq' is:
mcqs.why: The lesson defines it: 'haq' means an established thing and consideration. 'The literal meaning of haq is justice' is marked False in the lesson.

mcqs.q: How many kinds of rights are there?
mcqs.why: There are two kinds of rights: (1) Huqooq-Allah — the rights of Allah, and (2) Huqooq-ul-Ibad — the rights of fellow servants, the duties Allah made obligatory upon servants towards one another.

mcqs.q: What does the Quran command about relatives? (Bani Isra'il: 26)
mcqs.why: Allah says: 'And give relatives their right.' Relatives' rights include sharing their joys and sorrows, treating them well and helping them in difficult times.

mcqs.q: Breaking ties with relatives is:
mcqs.why: Keeping ties joined with relatives has been commanded, and breaking ties is strictly forbidden — the lesson adds: one who breaks ties will not enter Paradise. 'Breaking ties has been commanded' is False.

mcqs.q: How did the Prophet ﷺ treat his foster mother Bibi Halimah Sa'diyah (RA)?
options: He spread his cloak for her and sent her off with gifts
mcqs.why: This is the lesson's practical example of relatives' rights: he ﷺ would spread his cloak for her, speak to her attentively, and send her off with love and many gifts.

mcqs.q: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should ______.'
mcqs.why: The hadith of the lesson: 'Whoever believes in Allah Almighty and the Last Day should honour his guest.' In a good society the guest is honoured, and hospitality is the Sunnah of the Prophets.

mcqs.q: In the rights of a guest, what distinction must NOT be made?
mcqs.why: The rights of a guest include honouring him and looking after his comfort, making no distinction between Muslim and non-Muslim in these rights. The guest, too, should look after his host.

mcqs.q: When someone falls ill, one should:
options: Visit him without delay and pray for his recovery
mcqs.why: The rights of the sick: visit him, do not delay in visiting — because the sick person is often in pain — pray for his recovery, give him support and encouragement, and help him besides treatment.

mcqs.q: The Prophet ﷺ visited the sick:
options: Without distinguishing Muslim and non-Muslim — even his enemies
mcqs.why: The Holy Prophet ﷺ would visit the sick without distinguishing between Muslim and non-Muslim, so much so that he visited even his enemies. Visiting the sick is pleasing to Allah Almighty.

mcqs.q: Among human relationships, who has the greatest importance in rights?
mcqs.why: The lesson marks this True: among human relationships, relatives have the greatest importance. That is why their rights are described first in this lesson.

lessons.title: Hazrat Aisha Siddiqa (RA)
lessons.notes_html:
Family

  • Hazrat Aisha Siddiqa (RA) belonged to the Banu Taym family.
  • Her father was Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA) and her mother was Umm Ruman (RA).
  • She was extremely intelligent from childhood, and her life was a model of piety, abstinence and noble character. Most of her time was spent in the service of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Marriage

Her nikah with the Holy Prophet ﷺ took place before the migration to Madinah, and her rukhsati (departure to her husband's home) took place after the migration to Madinah.

Her excellence

  • The Prophet ﷺ said: "Aisha holds among the women of the world the same excellence that thareed holds among broths." (Thareed is the meat broth in which pieces of bread are dipped; this way of eating was much liked in Arabia.)
  • Many verses of Surah Al-Noor were revealed about her truthfulness and piety.
  • She narrated more than two thousand ahadith from the Holy Prophet ﷺ.
  • She took part in battles and rendered services in Ghazwa Uhud and Ghazwa Banu Mustaliq.
  • The Prophet ﷺ also passed away in her chamber.

Passing away

Hazrat Aisha Siddiqa (RA) passed away on 17 Ramadan al-Mubarak, 58 AH. Her funeral prayer was led by Hazrat Abu Hurairah (RA), the governor of Madinah at that time, and she was buried at night in the Baqi al-Gharqad graveyard of Madinah. (She did not pass away in 50 AH.)

mcqs.q: Who were the father and mother of Hazrat Aisha Siddiqa (RA)?
options: Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA) and Umm Ruman (RA)
mcqs.why: Her father was Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA) and her mother was Umm Ruman (RA) — Umm Ruman's relation with her was that of the respected mother.

mcqs.q: Hazrat Aisha Siddiqa (RA) belonged to which family?
mcqs.why: The book's own exercise answer: she belonged to the Banu Taym family — the family of Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA).

mcqs.q: When did her rukhsati take place?
mcqs.why: Her nikah took place before the migration to Madinah, but her rukhsati (departure to the Prophet's ﷺ home) took place after the migration to Madinah.

mcqs.q: The Prophet ﷺ compared Hazrat Aisha's (RA) excellence among women to the excellence of ______ among broths.
mcqs.why: He ﷺ said: 'Aisha holds among the women of the world the same excellence that thareed holds among broths.' Thareed is the meat broth with pieces of bread dipped in it, much liked in Arabia.

mcqs.q: Verses about her truthfulness and piety were revealed in which Surah?
mcqs.why: Many verses were revealed in Surah Al-Noor of the Holy Quran about the truthfulness and piety of Hazrat Aisha Siddiqa (RA).

mcqs.q: How many ahadith did Hazrat Aisha Siddiqa (RA) narrate from the Prophet ﷺ?
mcqs.why: The fill-in answer of the lesson: she narrated more than two thousand ahadith from the Holy Prophet ﷺ — one of the greatest narrators among the Companions.

mcqs.q: In which battles did she take part and render services?
mcqs.why: The book's exercise answer: she took part in battles and rendered services in Ghazwa Uhud and Ghazwa Banu Mustaliq.

mcqs.q: When did Hazrat Aisha Siddiqa (RA) pass away?
mcqs.why: She passed away on 17 Ramadan al-Mubarak, 58 AH. 'She passed away in 50 AH' is marked False in the lesson.

mcqs.q: Who led her funeral prayer?
mcqs.why: Her funeral prayer was led by Hazrat Abu Hurairah (RA), who was the governor of Madinah at that time.

mcqs.q: Where was Hazrat Aisha Siddiqa (RA) buried?
options: In the Baqi al-Gharqad graveyard of Madinah
mcqs.why: She was buried at night in the Baqi al-Gharqad (Jannat-ul-Baqi) graveyard of Madinah. Note: the Prophet ﷺ was buried in her chamber, but she herself rests in Baqi.

lessons.title: Hazrat Fareeduddin Ganj Shakar (RA)
lessons.notes_html:
Name, titles and birth

  • His real name was Masood (not Abdullah), and his titles were "Fareeduddin" and "Ganj Shakar".
  • His father's name was Jamaluddin Sulaiman and his mother's name was Qamar Khatoon.
  • He was born in the village Kotwal of Multan in 579 AH (he was not born in Sindh).
  • He passed away at the age of 93 in Muharram al-Haram, 728 AH.
  • His shrine is in Pakpattan (Sahiwal Division).

His spiritual path

  • He memorized the Holy Quran at a young age.
  • He belonged to the Chishti order of the Sufis.
  • His murshid (spiritual guide) was Hazrat Qutbuddin Bakhtiar Kaki (RA), and he used to go to Delhi to receive spiritual benefit from him.
  • He kept regular time for zikr and azkaar and used to offer nafl prayers regularly.
  • He stayed away from kings.

His services and books

  • He brought the Jat and Rajput tribes living in Ajodhan to Islam.
