  • Three of his books became most famous: "Mahiyat-e-Qalb", "Rahat-ul-Quloob" and "Asrar-ul-Auliya". People continue to benefit from these books to this day.

mcqs.q: What was the real name of Hazrat Baba Fareeduddin Ganj Shakar (RA)?
mcqs.why: His real name was Masood. 'His real name was Abdullah' is marked False. His father was Jamaluddin Sulaiman and his mother was Qamar Khatoon.

mcqs.q: What were his titles?
mcqs.why: His titles were 'Fareeduddin' and 'Ganj Shakar' — he is famous in the world by the name Baba Fareed Ganj Shakar.

mcqs.q: Where and when was he born?
options: In the village Kotwal of Multan, 579 AH
mcqs.why: He was born in a village 'Kotwal' of Multan in 579 AH. Both 'born in Sindh' (False) and 600 AH are wrong; Pakpattan is where his shrine is.

mcqs.q: Who was his murshid (spiritual guide)?
mcqs.why: His murshid was Hazrat Qutbuddin Bakhtiar Kaki (RA), and he used to go to Delhi to receive spiritual benefit from him.

mcqs.q: To which Sufi order did he belong?
mcqs.why: The lesson marks this True: Hazrat Fareeduddin Ganj Shakar (RA) belonged to the Chishti order of the Sufis.

mcqs.q: Which tribes living in Ajodhan did he bring to Islam?
mcqs.why: He brought the Jat and Rajput tribes living in Ajodhan to Islam. Ajodhan is the old name of the Pakpattan area where he settled.

mcqs.q: Which of these is one of his famous books?
mcqs.why: Three of his books became most famous: 'Mahiyat-e-Qalb', 'Rahat-ul-Quloob' and 'Asrar-ul-Auliya'. People continue to benefit from them to this day.

mcqs.q: At what age and in which year did he pass away?
mcqs.why: He passed away at the age of 93 in Muharram al-Haram, 728 AH. He had been born in 579 AH, which matches the age of 93 (in lunar years, closely).

mcqs.q: Where is his shrine?
mcqs.why: The fill-in answer of the lesson: his shrine is in Pakpattan (Sahiwal Division) — the city famous by his name to this day.

mcqs.q: What was his habit regarding kings?
mcqs.why: The lesson marks this True: Hazrat Fareeduddin Ganj Shakar (RA) stayed away from kings. Like the true Sufis, he kept his life for Allah and the people, not for courts.

lessons.title: Salahuddin Ayyubi (RA)
lessons.notes_html:
Name and education

  • His real name was Yusuf bin Ayyub; he became famous as "Ayyubi" from his father's name, and "Salahuddin" was his title.
  • He was born in the Iraqi city of Tikrit.
  • He got his education from the mosques and madrasahs of the cities of Damascus and Baalbek.

The Crusades

  • The Third Crusade was fought in 1187 CE for the conquest of Bait-ul-Muqaddas (Jerusalem).
  • Sultan Salahuddin Ayyubi (RA) inflicted a crushing defeat on the combined power of the European Crusaders in the Third Crusade.
  • The Crusader king Raynald was constantly breaking treaties with the Muslims of Palestine (he did not abide by the treaty).
  • The famous commander Richard of Britain also took part on the Crusader side (he was not an American commander).

His noble character

  • He announced a general amnesty for all the Christians of Palestine.
  • When an enemy like Richard fell ill, Sultan Salahuddin (RA) went for his inquiry after health (sent his own physician/came to ask after him).
  • Due to his good treatment, many Christians became Muslims; of the old and disabled Christians, the jizya was paid by Sultan Salahuddin (RA) himself.
  • Despite being Sultan, he spent his life with simplicity; he was never even the owner of the nisab of Zakat.
  • He made the empire spread from Egypt to Palestine into a welfare state.

Passing away

Sultan Salahuddin Ayyubi (RA) passed away in Damascus in 1193 CE, at the age of 57, due to a fever illness.

mcqs.q: What was the real name of Sultan Salahuddin Ayyubi (RA)?
mcqs.why: His real name was Yusuf bin Ayyub. He became famous as 'Ayyubi' from his father's name Ayyub, and 'Salahuddin' was his title.

mcqs.q: From where did he get his education?
options: The mosques and madrasahs of Damascus and Baalbek
mcqs.why: Sultan Salahuddin Ayyubi (RA) got his education from the mosques and madrasahs of the cities of Damascus and Baalbek.

mcqs.q: In which Crusade did he crush the combined power of the European Crusaders?
mcqs.why: He inflicted a crushing defeat on the combined power of the European Crusaders in the Third Crusade, fought in 1187 CE for Bait-ul-Muqaddas.

mcqs.q: When was the Third Crusade fought, and for what?
options: 1187 CE, for the conquest of Bait-ul-Muqaddas
mcqs.why: The Third Crusade was fought in 1187 CE for the conquest of Bait-ul-Muqaddas (Jerusalem). 'The Third Crusade was fought in 1187 CE' is marked True.

mcqs.q: Which Crusader king was constantly breaking treaties with the Muslims of Palestine?
mcqs.why: The Crusader king Raynald was constantly breaking treaties — 'Raynald used to abide by the treaty' is marked False in the lesson.

mcqs.q: For all the Christians of Palestine, Sultan Salahuddin (RA) announced:
mcqs.why: After victory he announced a general amnesty for all the Christians of Palestine — the opposite of cruelty. Due to his good treatment, many Christians became Muslims.

mcqs.q: When his enemy Richard fell ill, what did Sultan Salahuddin (RA) do?
options: Went for his inquiry after health
mcqs.why: When an enemy like Richard fell ill, Sultan Salahuddin Ayyubi (RA) went for his health inquiry (sent help/physician). Such was his conduct even with enemies.

mcqs.q: Sultan Salahuddin (RA) made his empire, spread from Egypt to Palestine, into a ______ state.
mcqs.why: The fill-in answer: he made the empire spread from Egypt to Palestine into a welfare state. Yet he himself lived with simplicity and was never even the owner of the nisab of Zakat.

mcqs.q: Where was Sultan Salahuddin Ayyubi (RA) born?
mcqs.why: The lesson marks this True: Sultan Salahuddin Ayyubi (RA) was born in the Iraqi city of Tikrit. He later passed away in Damascus.

mcqs.q: When and where did he pass away?
options: 1193 CE, in Damascus, at the age of 57
mcqs.why: Sultan Salahuddin Ayyubi (RA) passed away in Damascus in 1193 CE, at the age of 57, due to a fever illness.

lessons.title: Allama Ibn Khaldun (RA)
lessons.notes_html:
Name, birth and death

  • His real name was Abdur Rahman bin Muhammad.
  • He was born in Tunis, a country of North Africa, in 732 AH, corresponding to 1332 CE.
  • He memorized the Holy Quran in childhood itself.
  • He got his early education and training from his father, Muhammad.
  • He passed away in Cairo (Egypt) in 808 AH, corresponding to 1406 CE. Most of his life was spent in Egypt.

His services

  • He was appointed to important political posts in three countries: Tunis, Andalus and Egypt.
  • He served as secretary and qazi (judge) in the courts of the Sultan of Tunis Abu Ishaq, the governor of Andalus Sultan Ibn al-Ahmar, and the king of Egypt Barquq.
  • He performed duty as a teacher in the world-famous institution Jamia Al-Azhar (not Damascus University).

His books and theories

  • His famous books are "Al-Muqaddimah" and "Tareekh Ibn Khaldun" (History of Ibn Khaldun).
  • He presented the theory that knowledge has two kinds, and that human life — 'Umraniyat (sociology) — has two basic and important principles.
  • Intellectual knowledge man acquires by using his own senses; his observations and experiences are presented in a scholarly style in his books, and research on his life and works is being done in great academic institutions.

mcqs.q: What was the real name of Allama Ibn Khaldun?
mcqs.why: His real name was Abdur Rahman bin Muhammad. His father, Muhammad, gave him his early education and training.

mcqs.q: Where and when was he born?
mcqs.why: He was born in Tunis, a country of North Africa, in 732 AH, corresponding to 1332 CE. The book's exercise options list Morocco, Libya and Algeria as wrong choices.

mcqs.q: In which three countries did he hold important posts?
mcqs.why: He was appointed to important political posts in Tunis, Andalus and Egypt. The statement naming Saudi Arabia, Libya and Syria is marked False in the lesson.

mcqs.q: On which posts did he serve in the courts of sultans?
mcqs.why: He served as secretary and qazi (judge) in the courts of the Sultan of Tunis Abu Ishaq, the governor of Andalus Sultan Ibn al-Ahmar, and the king of Egypt Barquq.

mcqs.q: His famous books are:
mcqs.why: The famous books of Allama Ibn Khaldun are 'Al-Muqaddimah' and 'Tareekh Ibn Khaldun' (History of Ibn Khaldun). The other titles named belong to Hazrat Fareeduddin Ganj Shakar (RA) and others.

mcqs.q: According to his theory, knowledge has how many kinds?
mcqs.why: The fill-in answer of the lesson: Allama Ibn Khaldun presented the theory that knowledge has two kinds — and likewise that human life has two basic and important principles in his theory of 'Umraniyat.

mcqs.q: Where did he perform his duty as a teacher?
mcqs.why: He performed duty as a teacher in the world-famous institution Jamia Al-Azhar. 'He taught at Damascus University' is marked False in the lesson.

mcqs.q: From whom did he get his early education?
mcqs.why: The book's exercise answer: he got his early education from his father, Muhammad — his father's name is also confirmed by the fill-in section.

mcqs.q: When and where did Allama Ibn Khaldun pass away?
mcqs.why: He passed away in Cairo (Egypt) in 808 AH, corresponding to 1406 CE. The last and most part of his life was spent in Egypt.

mcqs.q: What did he memorize in his childhood itself?
mcqs.why: The lesson marks this True: Allama Ibn Khaldun memorized the Holy Quran in childhood itself. His learning later made him the founder of the science of society ('Umraniyat).
